chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Nawfalī, from al-Sukūnī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was brought a Christian man who had become Muslim, and with him was a pig that he had roasted and garnished with basil. He said: “What led you to this?” The man said: “I became ill and craved meat.” So he said: “Why did you not turn to goat meat?” Then he said: “Had you eaten it, I would have carried out the hadd punishment upon you; but I will strike you a beating, so do not repeat it.” Then he beat him until he urinated.

key_terms.خِنْزِيرٌ: pig; pork, which is forbidden to eat
key_terms.لَحْمِ الْمَاعِزِ: goat meat, mentioned as a lawful alternative

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about the punishment for a Muslim who prepares or eats pork?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a case brought before Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام concerning a recent Muslim convert who had prepared pork. The narration highlights the prohibition of consuming forbidden food, while also showing a distinction between preparing it and actually eating it in the legal response described here.
